items.title: Add error boundary for SSL certificate failures
acceptance_criteria: ssl.SSLError and requests.exceptions.SSLError are caught in HTTP client
User receives helpful error message instead of Python traceback
Message suggests --verify=no for self-signed certificates when appropriate
All existing SSL tests pass
items.approach: Wrap requests.Session.send() calls in try/except to catch SSL errors and convert to user-friendly messages via ExitStatus.NETWORK_ERROR

items.title: Add error handling for plugin import failures
acceptance_criteria: Plugin import failures are caught and logged as warnings
Application continues running with remaining plugins
User is notified that some plugins failed to load
No change to successful plugin loading behavior
items.approach: Wrap plugin_manager.register() calls in try/except to catch ImportError and ModuleNotFoundError, log warnings via logging module instead of crashing

items.title: Improve DNS failure error handling
acceptance_criteria: All socket.gaierror subtypes are caught, not just EAI_AGAIN and EAI_NONAME
Each error code receives appropriate user-facing message
Test coverage for all DNS error scenarios
Existing DNS error tests continue to pass
items.approach: Audit existing socket.gaierror handling in core.py; expand to cover all errno codes with specific helpful messages

items.title: Add global exception handler in CLI entry points
acceptance_criteria: Unexpected exceptions are caught at CLI entry point
User sees friendly error message with exit code, not traceback
KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit continue to work as before
Logging captures full exception for debugging
items.approach: Add top-level try/except in main() function; catch Exception and convert to ExitStatus.ERROR with logged traceback

items.title: Add catch-all error handling in nested JSON parsing
acceptance_criteria: KeyError, IndexError, TypeError during JSON construction are caught
User receives error message referencing the nested JSON syntax
NestedJSONSyntaxError continues to work as designed
All existing nested JSON tests pass
items.approach: Add try/except blocks around JSON construction in interpret.py and parse.py, convert runtime errors to NestedJSONSyntaxError subclass or user message

items.title: Improve download resume error handling
acceptance_criteria: When server doesn't support resume (returns non-206 status), user is warned
Download proceeds from start instead of silently failing
User knows resume capability was not available
Existing download tests pass
items.approach: Check response status code after Range request; if not 206 Partial Content, log warning and reset download position

items.title: Add error handling for config file write failures
acceptance_criteria: OSError and PermissionError during config save are caught
User is notified of save failure with helpful message
Application falls back to in-memory config
User can still make HTTP requests even if config write fails
items.approach: Wrap config.save() calls in try/except to catch OSError/PermissionError and fall back to in-memory config with warning

items.title: Fix file handle leak in process_file_upload_arg
acceptance_criteria: File handles opened in process_file_upload_arg are properly closed
No resource leaks when processing multiple file uploads
Upload functionality unchanged
Existing upload tests pass
items.approach: Refactor process_file_upload_arg to return file path instead of open handle, or ensure caller uses context manager to close file

items.title: Add caching to GitHub API user lookup
acceptance_criteria: Repeated lookups for same user are cached
Cache size limited to 500 users (LRU eviction)
API call count reduced when processing large contributor lists
Cache hit/miss stats available via DEBUG mode

items.title: Batch GitHub API calls in fetch_missing_users_details
acceptance_criteria: Multiple user lookups combined into single API call where possible
API call count reduced from O(n) to O(log n) for typical contributor lists
Batch size respects GitHub API limits (typically 100 users per call)
Existing contributor fetch tests pass
items.approach: Refactor fetch_missing_users_details to batch github_username lookups using GitHub's search API with multiple username queries or graphql bulk fetch

items.title: Optimize set operations in merge_all_the_people
acceptance_criteria: Set intersection used instead of repeated membership checks
Algorithm complexity reduced from O(n*m) to O(n+m)
Contributor merging produces identical results
Existing contributor fetch tests pass
items.approach: Replace nested loops with set intersection: common_names = set(contributors.keys()) & committers; process in single pass

items.title: Add connection pooling to GitHub API requests
acceptance_criteria: requests.Session object reused for all API calls
HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling enabled
API call latency reduced for large contributor lists
Existing contributor fetch tests pass
items.approach: Create module-level requests.Session() object; reuse for all fetch() calls instead of creating new connection for each request

items.title: Optimize debug logging in contributors fetch
acceptance_criteria: DEBUG flag cached at module startup
os.getenv() called once instead of on every debug() call
Debug behavior unchanged when DEBUG=1
No performance impact when DEBUG disabled
items.approach: Add module-level DEBUG = os.getenv('DEBUG') == '1'; check boolean flag in debug() function instead of calling os.getenv()

items.title: Consolidate config and context modules
acceptance_criteria: Config (preferences, settings) clearly separated from Context (runtime state)
Single authoritative source for configuration
All imports of config and context modules continue to work
All existing tests pass
Code duplication between modules eliminated
items.approach: Merge httpie.context into httpie.config; rename internal config management to ConfigManager; move runtime state to separate Context class with explicit dependency injection

items.title: Extract RequestExecutor service from core.py
acceptance_criteria: HTTP execution logic separated from CLI orchestration
RequestExecutor coordinates client, sessions, downloads independently
core.py focuses on entry point error handling and orchestration
All existing tests pass
RequestExecutor is independently testable
items.approach: Create httpie/request_executor.py with RequestExecutor class; move HTTP client creation, request execution, session persistence, and download coordination from core.py; have core.py delegate to RequestExecutor

dependencies.reason: Global exception handler must be added after SSL error handling is in place to avoid double-catching
Global exception handler should be added after DNS error handling is improved to have consistent error handling patterns
Batching optimization builds on caching; caching must be in place first for batching to be effective
RequestExecutor needs clear separation of config/context before extracting execution logic

dedup_summary: No duplicates found across auditors. All findings are distinct. Architecture findings (F-c491918d, F-bea35acf, F-e9757918, F-b23efcd9, F-8461d1ce, F-9458d64f) deferred as Tier 0 refactoring with high risk and low immediate value.
summary: 15 actionable items across 4 execution levels prioritizing error handling (tier 1-2, level 0) before orchestration improvements (tier 3, levels 1-3). Error handling covers SSL, plugins, DNS, exceptions, JSON parsing, downloads, config, and file leaks. Performance optimizations target GitHub API usage in contributor scripts. Architecture consolidation (config/context merge, RequestExecutor extraction) deferred to later phase. 6 architecture findings deferred as low-immediate-impact refactoring.
